## Highlight: consumer groups

- `kite consume -g GROUP TOPIC` joins a Kafka 4.0 consumer-protocol group, shares partitions with other members, and resumes committed offsets. `-B` starts at the earliest offset only for partitions without a commit.
- kite commits offsets after flushing records to stdout, not after the downstream reader processes them. Without `-g`, consume does not commit offsets. (#97)
- `kite group list` and `kite group describe GROUP` inspect groups, committed offsets, and partition lag without changing offsets. Use `group list --all` to include classic groups. (#97)

## Highlight: read-committed consume by default

**Behavior change:** `kite consume`, with or without `-g`, now skips aborted transactions and reads only up to the last stable offset. Use `--read-uncommitted` to restore the previous behavior and read up to the high watermark, including open and aborted transactional records. Use the same isolation mode for all members of a group. (#99)

## Highlight: transactional produce

`kite produce --txn ID TOPIC` writes all of stdin in one transaction. It commits on EOF and aborts on errors or interrupts before commit is sent. If interrupted after the commit request is sent, kite exits 130 and reports an unknown outcome instead of attempting to abort. This mode requires idempotence and broker-side transaction partition verification, enabled by default in Apache Kafka 3.6+. (#100)

## Also
- Group tables now align columns on terminals. Piped output remains headerless TSV, and JSON output is unchanged. (#98)
- Improved multi-broker and leader-change recovery. Standalone consume retries the refreshed leader before treating the gap in records as idle.
